# Build: auto-recover-stuck-builds

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-13T11:45:11.111Z
> Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, FYI to phone per fix.

## What to build
Continue build "Auto-recover stuck builds" (auto-recover-stuck-builds) — Phase 1, model Fable.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-13 11:45):
"Brett: if anything stops working, the server/orchestrator fixes it automatically with no one asking. Detect builds marked running with no live session (killed exit 143, failed exit 1), reset and requeue them, retry failed sessions, keep every slot filled, FYI to phone per fix."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (2 left, ~20 min):
[ ] s1 (~10 min) Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
[ ] s2 (~10 min) Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
Read first: framework/core/build-recovery.mjs, framework/core/build-pipeline.mjs, framework/core/builds-store-schema.mjs, framework/schemas/build-recovery.json, framework/spec/fixtures/build-recovery.json, framework/spec/check-build-recovery.mjs
Tick each step right after its commit: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step auto-recover-stuck-builds <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link auto-recover-stuck-builds --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Fable phase. Work through every step of the phase in this one session: they are checkpoints, not separate tasks. As each step finishes, commit it on your branch, push, and tick it (orchestrator.mjs act step auto-recover-stuck-builds <stepId> done), then go straight on to the next; nothing is lost if the session dies, the next one starts at the first open step on the same branch. When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note auto-recover-stuck-builds "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

split.note: Split by Claude into 15 steps (2 Fable).

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

Lifecycle and docs: add uninstall coverage for the new data files, lifecycle markers, help and glossary descriptions for the new commands and settings, and a feature in the Shipped features ledger. Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

Lifecycle and docs: add uninstall coverage for the new data files, lifecycle markers, help and glossary descriptions for the new commands and settings, and a feature in the Shipped features ledger. Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

steps.text: Define the build-recovery@1 contract in framework/core/build-recovery.mjs. It covers: (1) the stuck states a build can be in (running with no live session, session killed with exit 143, session failed with exit 1, heartbeat stale, slot leaked); (2) what happens for each state (reset the step, requeue, retry the session, or park in Pending once the retry cap is reached); (3) the per-build retry counter and its backoff; (4) the recovery event record (build id, phase, cause, exit code, action, attempt, at); (5) a pure plan(builds, sessions, slots, now) function that returns actions and never runs side effects. Add the matching recovery fields to the builds@1 normaliser (normBuild keeps them), with a migration that defaults old records.
steps.why: New cross-surface contract and a builds@1 schema and migration change that the dispatcher, launcher and console all read

steps.text: Write golden fixtures and a checker for build-recovery@1. Cover each stuck state, the retry cap, backoff timing, a build whose live session is healthy (no action), and a build whose PR is merged (never requeued). Run the checker in the spec sweep.
steps.why: These fixtures are the conformance contract for the recovery planner

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It also writes a heartbeat file while the session runs, so the planner has real liveness data.

Add a session liveness reader in framework/cli/session-liveness.mjs. It joins the builds store's running builds with live PIDs, heartbeats, tmux sessions and the exit records from the previous step. It outputs the input that build-recovery plan() expects. Add a CLI: `session-liveness.mjs list --json`.

Add the recovery executor in apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/recover.mjs. It applies plan() actions through the builds store under its lock: set the stuck step back to todo, set status to queued with a recovery note, increment the retry counter, release leaked agent slots, and park the build in Pending with a reason once the cap is hit. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Wire recovery into the dispatcher. pipeline.mjs tick runs recover first on every tick, then fills every free agent slot from the Queue (loop until slots or the Queue run out, not one build per tick), and respects account and model routing. The axf-pipeline cron needs no change.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. Send each one through axf.notify@1 (AmberX app) as one plain line: what stuck, the exit code, what was done and the attempt number. Parked builds get a banner item instead of only a push.

Register a systems-check health@1 check, `builds-stuck`, with an auto-fix that runs recover. Under the Fix it yourself setting it defaults to on. It turns red only when a build is parked after the cap or when recovery itself fails.

Add Recovery settings to the Build orchestrator settings sub-tab, on framework controls: auto-recover on/off, max retries (default 3), stale heartbeat minutes, backoff, FYI per fix on/off. Include the settings level-toolbar entries. Store them as Claude settings keys under builds.recovery.*.

Add a Recovery log view in the Build orchestrator: the latest recovery events per build (cause, exit, action, attempt) and a PriorityTag on each row. Each build view shows a recovery badge. Use only tokens and framework controls (DataGrid, TabGroup).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.

Lifecycle and docs: add uninstall coverage for the new data files, lifecycle markers, help and glossary descriptions for the new commands and settings, and a feature in the Shipped features ledger. Run plugin-lifecycle check, catalog.mjs --check and check-theme/check-controls/check-toolbars/check-chrome-assets.

Submit the Recovery log and settings to UI Review with 3 options and shots. Run the full checks. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/auto-recover-stuck-builds.md, covering what was added, the stuck states handled and how each part is reached through deep link, REST, MCP, CLI and voice. Add the THREADS.md row, open the PR stating API reach, link the PR with builds-live.mjs, and add the PR to the merge queue.

Continue build "Combine merge queue into one PR" (combine-merge-queue-into-one-pr) — Phase 1, model Opus.

Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 10 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Checkpoints: Steps are checkpoints inside this ONE session, not separate tasks: work through them in order without stopping between them; when a step is finished, commit it on your branch, push, then tick it done before starting the next. Nothing is lost if the session dies: the next session picks up at the first open step on the same branch. Never ask for a new prompt or a relaunch per step.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. CLI: confirm <repo> <pr> [--wait], status <repo> <pr>, list.

Persistent pending-confirmation store + poller: record each merge call as pending-github-confirmation in the push-banner data dir, a tick that re-reads pending ones with backoff, flips them to merged or merge-unconfirmed after the timeout, and raises one health@1 banner item for unconfirmed merges.

Merge queue path: after each queue merge call, record pending-github-confirmation and only mark the stack entry merged (and trigger the one-per-stack redeploy) once merge-confirm says merged; unconfirmed entries stay in the queue as 'awaiting GitHub'.

Auto-land and console auto-merge paths (push banner, settings autoLand/autoMerge): route their merge calls through the same request → confirm flow; nothing reports 'merged' from the merge API's 200 alone.

GitHub client plugin + server merge gate: the github plugin's merge action and the console server's merge gate return status pending-github-confirmation with a confirm id, and the gate's 'merged' answer comes from merge-confirm only.

Scripts and builds: find every remaining merge caller (grep 'pulls/.*/merge', 'gh pr merge', mergePullRequest in deploy/, framework/cli/, apps/console-web/plugins/) and switch it to the flow; builds-live / builds-reconcile mark a build complete only on a confirmed merge.

Push banner UI: show 'Pending GitHub confirmation' (spinner chip, tokens only, framework Chip) on PR rows and merge-queue entries right after a merge call, then Merged (with merge commit link) or 'GitHub hasn't confirmed' with Recheck. Toolbar stays role=toolbar with tap-confirm.

API for the UI: REST GET /api/plugins/push-banner/merge-confirm (list + one), POST …/recheck; MCP plugin commands push_banner_mergeconfirm_list|get|recheck; CLI merge-confirm.mjs; voice action merge.recheck; console_show target push-banner/merge-confirm/<repo>#<pr> deep link.

Notifications + glossary: declare the 'merge unconfirmed' alert in push-banner notify.json, describe the new CLI/commands where defined so the glossary catalog picks them up, lifecycle markers on doc lines.

Tests: unit tests for the read-back (MERGED + commit on main, MERGED but commit missing, still OPEN, API error, timeout) with a fake GitHub; merge-queue and auto-merge tests asserting nothing is 'merged' before confirmation; run check-merge-confirm, check-theme, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, plugin-lifecycle check.

steps.text: Record the exit status of every headless session. claude-headless.sh traps the exit and writes the exit code, the signal (143 = SIGTERM), the end time and the account into a session status file under the agent-slots dir. It journals every action and publishes through builds-live.mjs. Add `--dry-run`.

Retry failed sessions on another worker. When the exit record shows a usage limit or an account error, the executor requeues the build with an account hint, so the dispatcher routes it to a different worker through claude-workers.mjs route.

Send an FYI to the phone for each fix. Declare a `build-recovered` notification type and a `build-recovery-parked` notification type in the plugin's notify.json. API parity for the Recovery log and settings. Link the build with builds-live.mjs link. Commit.

Fix #555's CI failures, part 1: the plugin's own checks (lifecycle markers, help or glossary ratchet, plugin-commands static routes, fixtures). Rerun each failing check locally until it passes. Commit.

Fix #555's CI failures, part 2: the framework and console sweep (check-theme, check-controls, check-toolbars, check-chrome-assets, tracker --check, console typecheck after a rebake). Reproduce with AXF_DATA_DIR=off. Commit.

Add the setting 'UI Review is a merge gate' (key uiReview.gate, default false) to the UI Review plugin settings. Have it read and write the owner-only Claude setting 'UI Review gate', so one value drives both. A missing value counts as false, and existing installs migrate to false. Commit.

Make the gate decision one function, gateOn() in the plugin server and review.mjs. When the gate is off, 'review.mjs state --pr <n> --exit-code' exits 0 with state 'filed (not a gate)', and the ui-review@1 capability's held() returns false. Submissions are still filed, never refused. Commit.

Make the merge queue and the push banner stop holding PRs or keeping them as drafts for UI Review when gateOn() is false. That covers the merge-queue.mjs readiness check, land.mjs, and the auto-PR draft flag. Add a unit test for both gate states. Commit.

UI: add a Switch 'UI Review is a merge gate' to Settings → Plugins → UI Review, on the framework Switch with tokens only and the level toolbar's Simple level. Under it, a status line: 'Off: items are filed for you to look at, PRs never wait.' Commit.

API for the switch: REST GET/POST /api/plugins/ui-review/gate returning {on, heldPrs[]}. Turning it on is personOnly, matching the owner-only Claude setting; turning it off and reading it are open to everyone. Add the MCP plugin commands ui-review_gate_get/set, the CLI 'review.mjs gate [on|off|status]', the voice action 'uireview.gate', and the deep link console_show target 'settings:plugins/ui-review#gate'. Commit.

Release command: 'review.mjs release-held [--pr n…] [--all]', REST POST /api/plugins/ui-review/release, MCP ui-review_release, voice 'uireview.release'. For each PR still held for UI Review, it marks the review item non-blocking (still filed), un-drafts the PR, and adds it to the merge queue with land.mjs queue add. It goes through the merge queue only and never merges. Has a dry-run. Commit.

Release Brett's held PRs now: run release-held for #557, #553, #541, #536, #518 and #517 (GitHub writes as axHub veto calls with a reason, where the session token can't do them). Record the result per PR in the report. Commit.

Tests: python and node tests for gateOn() defaults, state --exit-code in both gate states, personOnly on turning the gate on, release-held in dry-run and real mode against a fake GitHub, and REST, MCP and CLI giving the same answers. Commit.

Docs and rules: update the shared rule 'Every UI change goes to UI Review' and the CLAUDE.md UI Review line to say a hold applies only while the gate switch is on (default off). Update the plugin README and help, run the glossary catalog --check, then claude-sync sync. Commit.

UI Review submission for the settings switch: 3 options as settings assets in apps/console-web/plugins/ui-review/assets/settings/, with desktop and phone shots from vite preview, submitted with review.mjs submit --choices. With the gate off it is filed but does not block. Commit the assets.

Finish: run the full CI sweep locally. Write the report _claude/builds/reports/ui-review-gate-switch-default-off.md (what #555's failures were and how they were fixed, the release result per PR, and the API list: deep link, REST, MCP, CLI, voice). Add a THREADS.md row, push, open the PR (it replaces #555; close #555 with a link), add it to the merge queue, and tick the build.

Console screen and tab inventory: build a static index of every console view, nav entry and tab group, with addresses, labels and keywords, from the view registry, and export it for the server.

Settings inventory: every setting in the SettingsRegistry and in every plugin sub-tab gets an address with get/set and type and range validation. Owner-only Claude settings are marked personOnly and refused.

Button and function inventory: expose the existing console action registry, toolbar buttons and context-menu items as press targets. Destructive ones need an explicit confirm flag, and deciding actions (approve/deny) stay personOnly.

Plugin targets: address every plugin, its UI and settings tab, and add enable/disable through the plugin-manager engine. Report dependency effects (what needs it) in the result. Core plugins refuse disable with a reason.

Search index: one ranked search over screens, tabs, settings, buttons, plugins, help and everything currently loaded (grid rows, build steps, UI Review items, chat lines). Each hit carries its address so it can be pulled into focus.

Browser executor: the console page receives console-control commands over the existing relay channel and runs open/press/set/scroll/focus/search through the target registry. It highlights the result and returns a result plus a live state snapshot (screen, tab, scroll, focused row).

Server REST: add /api/console-control/targets, /state, /do, /search, /focus, /scroll and /plugins/{id}/enable|disable. Commands go to the open console session (Follow Amber channel), with a clear 'no console open' error and an open_url fallback link. Settings and plugin toggles that need no browser run server-side.

Server-side guards: personOnly and owner-only refusal, confirm for destructive actions, an audit log line per command, and a rate limit. Send veto-policy tags to axHub for state-changing verbs and leave navigation read-only.
MCP tools in mcp_server.py: console_control_targets, _state, _do, _search, _focus, _scroll and _plugin (enable/disable). Extend console_show/console_open to accept the new addresses.
CLI: add axf console do|state|targets|search|focus|scroll|plugin enable|disable to framework/cli/axf.mjs, calling the REST routes, with --json output.

Voice (AmberX): map phrases to console-control commands ('scroll down', 'open plugins settings', 'find <x>', 'show step 3 of <build>', 'disable plugin <y>', 'press <button>') through the console actions registry, with spoken confirmation of the result.
control@1 integration: register the console-control targets so that control@1 tokens and planner items can point at addresses, and add console actions console.control.* with descriptions.

Search palette UI: a framework command-palette (Ctrl+K or a banner chip) listing search hits. Picking one pulls it into focus. Use tokens and TabGroup/Button only. Its API is the search route: deep link ?axf-cmd=search&q=, state via console_control_state.
Backfill batch 1: add data-axf-target and settings ids to hand-drawn elements in the banner, nav, Settings and Terminal views that the framework hooks don't reach.
Backfill batch 2: Builds views (orchestrator, Pipeline, Pending, Queue, Build manager), so that every build row and step is focusable.
Backfill batch 3: the remaining plugin UIs (UI Review, Plan Studio, Breakroom, Shipped features, Glossary and others) and their grids.

Coverage CI check framework/cli/check-console-control.mjs. It fails when a view, tab group, toolbar, setting, plugin or DataGrid has no address. The ratchet baseline framework/spec/console-control-baseline.json can only go down. Wire it into CI.
Server tests: pytest for the REST routes and MCP tools (targets, state, do, search, plugin enable/disable, personOnly refusal, no-console error).
Executor tests: Playwright against vite preview. Open a tab, scroll, focus a grid row and a build step, set a setting, press a button and search-then-focus, asserting the reported state.
Parity test: the same command through REST, MCP, CLI and the voice intent gives identical results and state.
Docs: help entries and glossary descriptions for the new actions, CLI and MCP tools; _claude/memory/docs/console-control.md; a CLAUDE.md conventions line.

Run all the checks (fixtures, check-console-control, theme, controls, toolbars, chrome-assets, pytest, e2e, parity). Write the report _claude/builds/reports/full-api-and-voice-control-of-the-entire-console-every-tab-screen-setting-bu.md, add a THREADS.md row and open the PR stating how each feature is reached (deep link, state, actions, settings via REST, MCP, CLI and voice).

API parity for the Recovery log and settings. REST routes: GET /recovery (state, events, settings), POST /recovery/run (with dry_run), POST /recovery/settings, POST /recovery/retry/<id>, POST /recovery/park/<id>. Expose the same routes as MCP plugin commands. Add a console_show deep link target `builds/orchestrator/recovery`. Add the CLI `recover.mjs status|run|retry|park|settings` and voice actions `recovery.run`, `recovery.status` and `recovery.retry` for AmberX.

Write tests: run the executor against a temp builds store with fake exit records (143, 1, a stale heartbeat, a healthy session, the cap reached). Assert requeue, reset, slot release, park and notify calls, check that the tick fills all free slots, and run the routes smoke test. Add them to CI.
